text_blocks.snippet: While rare, Lyme disease can, in some instances, lead to stroke due to inflammation of blood vessels in the brain (cerebral vasculitis). This can occur as a complication of Lyme neuroborreliosis (LNB), a neurological form of Lyme disease. The inflammation can cause narrowing or blockage of arteries, leading to ischemic stroke.
